description: REQ-004 says 'post_reel.py's output JSON SHALL include a NEW key `outcome`' unconditionally (every output, all 3 values), and explicitly assigns 'failed' to cover 'the share button was never reached, i.e. the existing `reached` field never advanced to READY/past the composer steps'. But the real code has FIVE distinct early-return paths that never reach the share-click block at all and today simply `print(json.dumps(res)); return` with no outcome-equivalent field: not-logged-in (line 95), ACCOUNT GUARD abort (line 108), no-create-btn (line 127), file-chooser-load-failed (line 134), video-never-loaded (line 141). REQ-004/PROP-004/PROP-005 only describe wiring `classify_outcome` into the post-share flow (verification-architecture.md's pseudocode starts AFTER the composer/caption steps) and only test the `no-share-btn` early-return case (PROP-005 case 3) -- the other four early-return paths are never mentioned anywhere in either spec document, so nothing guarantees they get an `outcome` key at all after Phase 2, silently violating REQ-004's own 'SHALL include' language for those paths. REQ-005/006/007 also have no branch for 'outcome key absent/None' -- run.sh's 3-way routing is unspecified for this case.

evidence.snippet: res["error"] = "not logged in"; print(json.dumps(res)); return   /  res["error"] = f"ACCOUNT GUARD..."; ...print(...); return   /  res["error"] = "no create btn"; print(json.dumps(res)); return   /  res["error"] = "file chooser load failed"; ...return   /  res["error"] = "video never loaded"; ...return

additionalEvidence.note: the 'Concrete refactor' pseudocode only begins after the composer/caption flow completes -- it never shows classify_outcome (or any outcome assignment) wired into the 5 early-return failure paths listed above.
PROP-005 only tests the no-share-btn early-return shape, not the other 4 early-return paths.
